correctness.rationale: The rank-one projection P_{(i,j),(k,l)}=delta_ik/b+delta_jl/a-1/(ab) is an exact orthogonal projection onto the graph cut space. The classical transfer-current determinant gives the exact covariance C(e,f)=-P(e,f)^2 off diagonal. Its four invariant tensor sectors yield all eigenvalues, while the 2x2 constant/mean block gives exactly one zero eigenvalue. Algebra proves the min/max eigenvalue formula. Finite orders four through fifteen optimizers follow exhaustive exact-rational comparison; all orders at least sixteen exclusion follows explicitly from (a-4)(b-4)>=0, the explicit positive large-order quadratic, and the second positive large-order quadratic. Exact enumeration on six small graphs corroborates, not proves, the all-n theorem. See RESULT.md and verify.py.

originality.rationale: Bounded published-record, previous mathematical-claim, and primary-paper searches did not identify the precise complete first-Walsh-band Gram spectrum and all-order fixed-vertex bipartition optimum. Previously known determinantal spanning-tree formulas imply individual covariance entries and are explicitly excluded from originality; extracting and optimizing the sharp spectral invariant is the newly assessed theorem. The principal residual possibility is an earlier equivalent covariance-eigenspace or optimal-design formulation.
residual_risks: Generic forest-containment formulas algebraically determine the entries, so an earlier spectral corollary under different terminology could supersede the claim.
Lyons complete preprint was not materially inspected beyond its abstract; general framework claims are not asserted absent from that full text.
Published-record search and inspected sources do not constitute a universal priority guarantee.

value.rationale: The fixed-order bipartition is a natural experimental-design variable for stable first-coordinate Walsh reconstruction under a spanning-tree constraint. The finding gives the complete nonzero Gram spectrum and a sharp all-n optimum, with a balanced optimum at order eight, a two-shape tie at order nine, a 3-versus-(n-3) phase through order fourteen, and a permanent thin-side optimum at all orders at least fifteen. The balanced squared condition grows as one-thirty-second of the cube of the order, whereas the attainable minimum grows only as n, a structural and quantitatively substantial gap.
